channel.title: GUI Agents Papers
channel.description: A curated, searchable list of research papers on GUI agents — models, frameworks, benchmarks, datasets, and more.

item.title: Adaptation of Computer Use Agents to New Software with User Manuals
item.description: Proposes MAGE, a framework that utilizes application user manuals to generate explicit procedural guidance during inference and self-guided rollouts for training, improving computer-use agent generalization to unseen desktop software.

item.title: MobileInject: Evaluating Reasoning-to-Action Security of MLLM-Based Mobile Agents under Cross-Modal Consistency Injection
item.description: Introduces MobileInject, a benchmark evaluating multimodal mobile agents against Cross-Modal Consistency Injection attacks across 11 scenarios and 9 security-risk categories to identify early-stage reasoning hijacking.

item.title: MobileJailBench: Red Queen Jailbreak Benchmarking for Mobile Agents
item.description: Presents MobileJailBench, a dynamically evolving jailbreak benchmark comprising 520 tasks across 14 risk categories on a realistic mobile sandbox to evaluate mobile agent vulnerabilities against multi-step jailbreak attacks.

item.title: PersonaCUABench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents Serving Diverse Personas
item.description: Introduces PersonaCUABench, an evaluation suite assessing computer-use agents across 44 user personas to examine how colloquial expressions, ambiguous constraints, and personalized requirements degrade agent success in desktop environments.

item.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
item.description: Introduces LEASH, a training-free weak-to-strong escalation framework for computer-use agents that uses internal hidden state uncertainty to dynamically trigger handoff to a strong model and supervise it via a shadow observer on OSWorld.

item.title: Not All Graphs Are Maps: A Task-Agnostic Exploration Framework for Mobile GUI Navigation
item.description: Presents TAG-Nav, a task-agnostic exploration framework creating persistent graph memory of mobile app destinations, and DestBench, a navigation benchmark isolating destination discovery from task completion.

item.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
item.description: Proposes OS-Helix, an end-to-end trained multimodal computer-using agent uniting GUI actions and bash code execution in one unified action space, trained with Step-balanced GSPO on live desktop environments and achieving 66.44% on OSWorld-Verified.

item.title: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use
item.description: Introduces OpenGCUA, an open stack for generalist computer-use agents that integrates visual GUI action with programmatic code execution, demonstrating substantial partial-score gains across eight frontier models on OSWorld-v2.

item.title: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
item.description: Proposes Intact, a web agent defense architecture that leverages browser origin and structural semantics through GenTree to isolate untrusted web elements and block visual prompt injection attacks during autonomous web browsing.

item.title: How GUI Agents Fail: GraceBench for Execution Stability Diagnosis
item.description: Introduces GraceBench, an online evaluation benchmark that maps mobile apps as UI Transition Graphs (UTGs) to diagnose step-level execution stability, measuring deviation, loop burden, and recovery dynamics beyond binary task success.

item.title: MAI-Gym: An Open All-in-One Platform for GUI Agent Evaluation and RL Training across Mobile and Computer Environments
item.description: Presents MAI-Gym, an open platform unifying GUI agent evaluation, task synthesis, and online RL across mobile and computer environments, scaling to 20,000 parallel instances and training a 9B model that scores 78.4% on MobileWorld and 76.2% on OSWorld-Verified.

item.title: MMA-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Agent Safety Evaluation
item.description: Presents MMA-SafetyBench, a safety benchmark assessing Visual Semantic Hijacking in multimodal agents through 1,083 adversarial trajectories spanning web automation, desktop GUI, mobile navigation, and document tasks.

item.title: STP-GUI: Spatially-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Web-GUI Agents
item.description: Presents STP-GUI, a spatially aware token pruning method that identifies task-critical web elements and discards redundant background visual tokens, reducing computational latency while preserving navigation accuracy on WebArena.

item.title: Task-State Governance: A Virtual Machine for Verifiable and Recoverable GUI Agent Execution
item.description: Proposes task-state governance and TaskVM, an interaction virtual machine that represents GUI agent tasks as editable contracts linking desired outcomes and application states, enabling verifiable execution and user-controlled error recovery.

item.title: Teaching Agents in their Own Style: Blackbox Teacher Distillation for Web Agents
item.description: Proposes a blackbox distillation framework for web agents where student models generate candidate plans and a closed teacher model edits them into the student's formatting style, substantially improving performance on WebArena and Mind2Web without access to teacher logits.

item.title: Why Generate a Click? Plug-in Decision Heads for Web Agents
item.description: Analyzes token generation overhead in web agents and proposes replacing autoregressive action text generation with specialized plug-in classification and regression decision heads, speeding up inference and improving action accuracy on WebArena.

item.title: Adaptive-Group Process Rewards for GUI Agents
item.description: Introduces Adaptive-Group Process Rewards to address sparse outcome rewards in GUI agent reinforcement learning. By grouping correlated interaction steps and computing adaptive process rewards on intermediate sub-goals, the method improves credit assignment and sample efficiency across desktop and web navigation benchmarks.

item.title: GroundGUI: GUI Grounding by High-Quality Data and Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Introduces ScreenRef, a high-quality multi-platform GUI referring expression dataset, and GroundGUI, an agent trained via distillation from large VLMs followed by reinforcement learning, achieving superior grounding accuracy across desktop, web, and mobile environments.

item.title: Interaction-as-a-Judge
item.description: Proposes Interaction-as-a-Judge, an evaluation paradigm where computer-use agents actively interact with web applications, desktop software, and games to evaluate interactive functionality. Releases 6,858 application-trace pairs and 222 human-verified requirement benchmarks, demonstrating improved alignment with human quality assessments over static code-based evaluation.

item.title: Learning How to Remember: Memory Modality Selection for GUI Agents
item.description: Investigates memory representations in GUI agents and discovers that optimal memory modality (textual summary, action sequence, or screenshot embeddings) varies dynamically across task stages. Introduces SwitchMem, a policy that dynamically selects the memory modality for retrieved experience, boosting task success on OSWorld and Mind2Web.

item.title: MHVF: Training-Free GUI Grounding via Verification-Guided Multi-Hypothesis Search
item.description: Proposes Multi-Hypothesis Verification and Filtering (MHVF), a training-free inference framework that generates diverse candidate click points and filters them through bidirectional verification between instruction intent and visual context. MHVF achieves substantial grounding accuracy gains on WebVoyager and ScreenSpot without additional model fine-tuning.

item.title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: Proposes CarryOn, an object-oriented context runtime that organizes agent continuation around reusable task objects rather than raw interaction history. On OSWorld 2.0 and BrowseComp-Plus, CarryOn improves success rates by 5.8% and 7.0% while slashing token usage by 51.9% and 22.9%.

item.title: Towards Safe Autonomy for Computer Use
item.description: Investigates safety architectures for computer-use agents subjected to indirect prompt injection. Analyzes the failure modes of safety classifiers and proposes capability-bounded execution policies with information-flow tracking, ensuring that untrusted web and application inputs cannot trigger unauthorized system actions.

item.title: BrowseSafe++: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detection Across Web Contexts, Languages, and Browser Views
item.description: Introduces BrowseSafe++, an expanded benchmark of 38,675 webpage pairs evaluating prompt injection detection across diverse web contexts, multilingual content, and rendered browser views. Assesses commercial and open detector models, highlighting critical detection gaps when injections exploit visual DOM structures.

item.title: HyWe: Unifying Search and Operation for Real-World Hybrid Web Tasks
item.description: Proposes HyWe, a unified framework integrating broad information retrieval and deep interactive page navigation within a single agent trajectory. Equipped with mode-switching policies and specialized tool harnesses, HyWe substantially improves success on complex hybrid web tasks compared to isolated search or navigation agents.

item.title: Learn from Move: the Next Step for GUI Agents
item.description: Focuses on enabling GUI agents to autonomously explore and learn unfamiliar software interfaces through interactive trial and feedback. Introduces an exploration-driven learning protocol and benchmark where agents discover hidden menu actions and state semantics, improving generalization to unseen desktop applications.

item.title: PrivacyGuard: Source-Linked Sanitization and Locally Resolvable PII References for Cloud GUI Agents
item.description: Presents PrivacyGuard, a client-side privacy architecture for cloud-backed GUI agents that replaces personally identifiable information (PII) in instructions and screenshots with source-linked synthetic tokens. Using locally resolvable references, the agent completes tasks on remote cloud planners without leaking sensitive personal data.

item.title: Seg2Click: Learning Pixel-Level Action Masks for GUI Visual Grounding
item.description: Reformulates GUI visual grounding as executable-region prediction, training models with bounding-box supervision to output pixel-level action masks rather than single-point coordinates. Seg2Click avoids visual-token grid misalignment and achieves higher localization accuracy on fine-grained and dense interface targets.

item.title: A Decade in a Day: Synthesizing Agent-Native Interfaces from Human-Oriented Software Evolution
item.description: Investigates how software evolution impacts agent usability and introduces DeskIF-Bench across six desktop applications, along with ANIS, a framework synthesizing agent-native interfaces from installed software capabilities to enhance success rates and reduce token costs.

item.title: The Agent Clicks Approve: Injected Page Text Makes Browser Agents Authorize Access the Task Never Named
item.description: Demonstrates a confused-deputy attack against browser agents acting in authenticated sessions, where adversarial text on a visited page steers the agent into approving third-party OAuth access or registering malicious webhook endpoints. Testing across commercial and open-source browser agents reveals high vulnerability rates to unprompted privilege escalation.

item.title: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack
item.description: Introduces MASTIF, an evaluation framework assessing combinations of 3 LLMs, 3 communication protocols, and 4 agent implementation frameworks across 300 Mind2Web benchmark tasks. Provides systematic baseline metrics on task completion, execution time, and communication verbosity across alternative agentic web stacks.

item.title: CaptchaAgent: Verifiable Visual Reasoning for CAPTCHA Solving
item.description: Presents CaptchaAgent, an agent framework for reasoning-intensive CAPTCHAs combining count-committed visual perception with verified browser interaction. Evaluated across diverse modern CAPTCHA suites, CaptchaAgent improves Pass@1 by 21.3-25.8 percentage points over standard VLM baselines.

item.title: ConClick: Element-Wise Contrastive Learning Improves GUI Grounding
item.description: Analyzes GUI grounding error patterns and identifies that incorrect clicks predominantly land on plausible distractor elements rather than background. Proposes ConClick, a contrastive learning framework trained on 4,292 target-distractor pairs, improving Qwen3-VL-8B grounding accuracy from 54.7% to 66.0% on ScreenSpot-Pro and from 63.3% to 70.2% on OSWorld-G.

item.title: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents
item.description: Proposes Latent World Action Model (LWAM) for GUI agents, shifting screen transition prediction from expensive pixel reconstruction into a compact latent visual space. LWAM enables efficient forward rollouts and action evaluation, achieving 4.8x faster inference and improved action selection accuracy on OSWorld and AndroidWorld.

item.title: OpenMobile-2: Building Versatile Mobile Agents with Scalable Environments and App-Native Tools
item.description: Presents OpenMobile-2, an open mobile agent trained on MobileGym++, which features 35 realistic simulated commercial applications with interactive environments and app-native tools. OpenMobile-2 achieves frontier performance across diverse mobile benchmarks while releasing open training recipes and environment sandboxes.

item.title: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
item.description: Introduces Web$hell, a unified web access interface that compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects via WebContract, maintaining them in WebCache. Web$hell unifies broad information gathering and fine-grained browser interaction, improving task success while lowering interaction costs on Mind2Web and web search benchmarks.

item.title: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
item.description: Introduces a paired benchmark of 280 executable web agent tasks assessing susceptibility to misleading visual charts and deceptive dashboard designs. Demonstrates that frontier multimodal web agents frequently misinterpret truncated axes and inverted scales, making erroneous navigation and purchasing decisions.

item.title: Work2Skill: Capturing Human GUI Experience for Reusable Agent Skill Induction
item.description: Introduces Work2Skill, a pipeline for inducing modular and parameterized skills from human GUI demonstration recordings. By parsing GUI action trajectories and abstracting environment-specific element locators, Work2Skill improves execution success on complex desktop workflows in OSWorld while reducing demonstration collection costs.

item.title: AgentHorizon: Evaluating Agentic Judges for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Tasks
item.description: Presents AgentHorizon, a benchmark and diagnostic suite evaluating automated agentic judges on multi-application, long-horizon computer-use trajectories from OSWorld and WorkArena. Shows that current VLM judges suffer significant false-positive rates on complex multi-window workflows due to temporal aggregation errors and misread intermediate states.

item.title: DeltaReplay: Task-Relative Memory Reuse for Mobile GUI Agents
item.description: Proposes DeltaReplay, a memory-augmented framework for mobile GUI agents that represents historical trajectories as paths in a state transition graph and reuses them relative to task differences. Evaluated on AndroidWorld, DeltaReplay avoids rigid replay failures and reduces execution steps by dynamically adapting past trajectories to new target parameters.

item.title: Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling: When Weight Training Should Begin
item.description: Analyzes the trade-off between self-evolving agent harnesses and weight training for long-horizon agents, showing that harness evolution fixes process failures (loops, budget exhaustion) while weight training is necessary for content failures. Validates the diagnosis rule across DeepPlanning and WebArena-Lite (+0.09 on 117 unseen tasks).

item.title: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
item.description: Formulates GUI agent safety as transition verification rather than static screen inspection, noting that identical screens can be benign or malicious depending on the preceding action. Introduces a world-model-based transition verifier that predicts expected screen changes and flags anomalous or redirected transitions across Android and web benchmarks.

item.title: SoftwareGym: Scaling Computer-Use Agent Training with Diverse Synthesized Software Environments
item.description: Introduces SoftwareGym, a platform that scales computer-use agent training by synthesizing diverse desktop software applications and programmatic verifiers. Pre-training agents with reinforcement learning across 1,200+ synthesized software environments substantially boosts out-of-domain transfer performance on OSWorld.

item.title: Adversarial Images Hijack Web Agents from Visual Grounding to Browser Execution
item.description: Studies end-to-end visual adversarial attacks targeting multimodal web agents from visual grounding down to browser execution. Demonstrates that imperceptible adversarial image perturbations on webpages consistently hijack agent attention and cause targeted misclicks across Mind2Web and VisualWebArena.

item.title: Secure-CUA: Controlling Untrusted Influence in Computer-Use Agents
item.description: Introduces Secure-CUA, a security framework that isolates untrusted interface content from computer-use agent planning across desktop, web, and mobile environments. By enforcing information-flow constraints on UI elements and restricting actions derived from untrusted inputs, Secure-CUA prevents indirect prompt injection while preserving legitimate automation capabilities.

item.title: AdvSim2Real : Training Web Agents Against Adaptive Prompt Injection in a Web World Model
item.description: Proposes AdvSim2Real, an adversarial simulation framework that trains web agents against adaptive indirect prompt injection within a web world model sandbox. Pre-training agents against simulated adversarial web pages significantly reduces injection vulnerability on live web benchmarks without harming benign navigation success.

item.title: Can Agents Work for Everyone? Cross-User Reliability for Mobile GUI Agents in Personalized User Interfaces
item.description: Introduces PAIR, a benchmark evaluating mobile GUI agents across personalized interface states resulting from diverse user histories and configurations. Proposes RePAIR, a reinforcement learning method with personalization-aware interaction rewards that improves agent robustness against UI layout shifts across distinct user accounts.

item.title: nanoMuse: An Open-Source Personal Agent for Every Device You Own
item.description: Analyzes the architecture of proprietary cross-device personal assistants and presents nanoMuse, an open-source cross-device agent operating on phone and computer screens. It features a shared cross-device session relay, a safety Sentinel gating screen actions, and transparent file-based provenance memory.

item.title: AMBER: Training Long-Horizon Web Agents through Append-Only Memory
item.description: Proposes AMBER (Append-only Memory Bank for Evidence Retention), an architecture that replaces overwrite memory mechanisms with structured append-only evidence recording for long-horizon web navigation. AMBER prevents critical historical evidence and error feedback from being discarded during multi-step execution, boosting task completion across WebArena and WorkArena.

item.title: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling
item.description: Presents CLIFT, a framework applying conformal prediction to provide calibrated step-level self-verification signals for web agents without relying on costly external LLM judges. Used for RL credit assignment and test-time trajectory search, CLIFT yields consistent success rate gains on WebArena and Mind2Web.

item.title: Decoupling What from Where: How Should a Small GUI Grounding Model Receive the Action Type?
item.description: Investigates whether small GUI grounding models (Qwen2-VL-2B) should receive action type information explicitly or infer it jointly with coordinates on Android in the Wild. Finds that conditioning coordinate prediction on the action type through decoupled embeddings improves grounding accuracy while reducing parameter overhead.

item.title: Imagine to Act: High-Fidelity Data Synthesis via Image Editing World Model for Scalable GUI Agent Training
item.description: Proposes Imagine to Act, an image-editing world model framework that synthesizes high-fidelity GUI transition trajectories by generating post-action screenshots from localized element manipulations. Fine-tuning vision-language models on the synthesized trajectories substantially improves multi-step execution and grounding performance across Android and desktop GUI benchmarks.

item.title: PlaySuite: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Interactive Visual Intelligence
item.description: Introduces PlaySuite, a benchmark evaluating interactive visual agents across 5K+ open-source video games (Pygame, HTML5, Godot, Unity) using a closed-loop execution harness and Video-LLM judge. Evaluation of 14 vision-language models and computer-use agents reveals a substantial perception-action gap, with agents failing consistently on dynamic spatial grounding and real-time self-correction.

item.title: Recurrent Latent Visual Search for GUI Grounding
item.description: Proposes Recurrent Latent Visual Search (RLVS) for GUI grounding, addressing single-step grounding failures on crowded screenshots by iteratively refining latent target representations across recurrent search steps. RLVS improves grounding accuracy across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces without relying on explicit bounding box prompts.

item.title: TeleTune: Evolving Agent Skills From Offline Telemetry
item.description: Introduces TeleTune, a framework that induces reusable textual skill libraries for computer-use agents from offline user telemetry logs without goal labels or replayability. Guided by action-prediction error reductions on logged trajectories, TeleTune achieves 77.1% on WorkArena and 80.6% on Online-Mind2Web, outperforming Agent Workflow Memory by 6.7-7.7% while consuming up to 75x fewer tokens than live optimization.

item.title: MedImageOSWorld: Benchmarking GUI Agents for Medical Image Consoles
item.description: Introduces MedImageOSWorld, a benchmark evaluating GUI agents on simulated CT, MR, and ultrasound console interfaces across seven capability levels using mouse-and-keyboard interactions. Testing eleven open-weight and two proprietary agents reveals that open-weight models achieve only 3.0-25.0% procedural success and collapse on fine-grained planning and closed-loop acquisition control.

item.title: CUAWright: A Minimal Unified Interface for Digital Agents
item.description: Proposes CUAWright, a minimal (~3K LOC) terminal-based execution harness using bash commands and file-system evolution as the interface for digital agents, arguing that GUI-native harnesses limit programmatic operations. On OSWorld 2.0, CUAWright improves partial reward by 33.2% while reducing token cost by 37.5% over the GPT-5.5 baseline, and achieves +4.7% and +44.0% success rate gains on Online-Mind2Web and Odysseys.

item.title: Control OSWorld: An AI Control Environment for GUI Computer Use Agents
item.description: Introduces Control OSWorld, an evaluation pairing 318 tasks from OSWorld with 81 harmful side tasks (such as private file exfiltration) that a computer-use agent must complete without detection. Evaluates monitors that detect malicious GUI actions, finding that full-trajectory monitors achieve 97% recall at a 3% false positive rate, whereas step-level monitors suffer lower recall due to reduced context.

item.title: Securing Computer-Use Agents Against Branch Steering Attacks
item.description: Studies branch steering attacks, in which untrusted page content pushes a computer-use agent down a hazardous but pre-approved branch of a Dual-LLM plan without injecting explicit instructions, and introduces STEER-Bench (101 tasks across 9 domains) to measure them. Proposes COBRA, which pairs trusted branching plans with ahead-of-time capability constraints on the parameters and destinations each branch may use; it reduces attack success on STEER-Bench to 0% while retaining 97% benign utility.

item.title: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites
item.description: Technical report of WebFovea, a vision-based web agent that placed 2nd in the WebRetriever Challenge 2026 on live websites. Many failures it observed occur in the harness between the model and the browser (action parsing, action execution, result reporting, and observation) rather than in model reasoning; hardening each stage raised the official hidden-set score from 31.0 to 57.0 with the same model.
